---
title: "Canonical Identities and Schemas"
subtitle: "Which bytes name a Plan, request, attempt, Result, and receipt?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** `CONVERGING` implementation design. The
[machine-readable V1 schema bundle](../../src/scnsim/_schemas/identity-v1.schema.json) is the
field-and-type authority for this page.

The bundle is shipped once as `scnsim/_schemas/identity-v1.schema.json` and
located through `importlib.resources`; the documentation site publishes that
same package-resource byte stream rather than maintaining a copy.

## Encode one canonical byte stream

Python owns canonical serialization. It converts physical inputs to coherent
SI and finite IEEE-754 binary64, then writes each physical floating scalar as
its 16 lowercase big-endian hexadecimal bits. Counts, booleans, identities,
and enum values keep their declared JSON types. Complex quantities store
separate real and imaginary bit strings. This avoids Python/Julia
decimal-printer differences while preserving one exact numerical value.

Every document is UTF-8, normalizes strings and object keys to NFC, orders
object keys lexicographically, and contains no insignificant whitespace. Key
normalization collisions fail closed. Every envelope contains `schema` and
integer `schema_version` discriminators; canonical key ordering determines
their byte position. SHA-256 covers the complete canonical document; no
document contains its own recursive hash. NaN, infinity, pickle, absolute
paths, `..`, backslashes, and symlink escapes are invalid before any hash or
artifact read.

Arrays whose order is physical—Ports, pins, coordinates, lineage steps, modes,
and axes—retain that order. Set-like collections sort by their canonical
identity. A typed map stores lexicographically ordered string-key entries;
duplicate keys fail before serialization.

For the full-V1 Plan schema, that rule is mechanical rather than inferred:

| Array | Canonical order |
|---|---|
| `catalog_sources` | ascending `catalog_id` |
| `components` and nested `children` | ascending lexicographic `component_path` segment array |
| component `parameter_bindings` and `inductive_branches` | ascending declared `id` |
| Composite `public_parameters` | factory declaration order |
| Composite `public_pin_map`, `public_coordinate_map`, and `public_inductive_branch_map` | ascending `public_id` |
| Composite `public_parameter_maps`; each map's `consumers` | ascending public `(component_path, parameter_id)`; ascending target `(component_path, parameter_id)` |
| component `pin_order` | Library-schema declaration order |
| `nodes` | ascending `node_id` |
| node `endpoints` and `grounded_endpoints` | ascending `(component_path, pin_id)` |
| `ports` | Plan declaration order |
| Plan and Composite `couplings` | ascending coupling `id` |

Every canonical identity in those set-like collections is unique; duplicates
fail closed. `pin_order`, Ports, and `QuantitySum.terms` remain declaration
ordered because their order carries public meaning.

An anonymous non-Port node hashes the canonical envelope
`{"schema":"scnsim.internal_node","schema_version":1,"endpoints":[...]}`,
where `endpoints` uses the order above. Its opaque evidence identity is
`internal-<sha256>`, retaining all 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. Public IDs
cannot use that reserved shape. This makes the identity independent of
`plan.net()` call order without treating an Internal node as a selectable API.

The full-V1 quantity vocabulary is also closed. SCNSim never serializes a Pint
formatter's current spelling:

| Physical kind | `si_unit` | `dimensionality` |
|---|---|---|
| capacitance | `farad` | `capacitance` |
| inductance | `henry` | `inductance` |
| resistance | `ohm` | `resistance` |
| conductance or root slope | `siemens` | `conductance` |
| ordinary frequency or linewidth | `hertz` | `inverse_time` |
| complex angular frequency | `radian / second` | `inverse_time` |
| current | `ampere` | `current` |
| voltage | `volt` | `voltage` |
| length | `meter` | `length` |
| resistance per length | `ohm / meter` | `resistance_per_length` |
| inductance per length | `henry / meter` | `inductance_per_length` |
| conductance per length | `siemens / meter` | `conductance_per_length` |
| capacitance per length | `farad / meter` | `capacitance_per_length` |
| Direct dynamic operator | `siemens / second` | `conductance_per_time` |
| HB node-flux coefficient | `weber` | `magnetic_flux` |
| S or optimizer coordinates | `dimensionless` | `dimensionless` |

An extension that needs another physical kind must extend the schema rather
than insert a locally formatted unit string.

Runtime algorithms are likewise closed for full V1:

| Operation | `algorithm_id` |
|---|---|
| Direct S/Y/Z | `scnsim.direct_response.v1` |
| diagonal root | `scnsim.diagonal_root.newton32.v1` |
| hybridized pole | `scnsim.hybridized_pole.newton32.v1` |
| transfer zero | `scnsim.transfer_zero.newton32.v1` |
| residue-normalized coupling | `scnsim.residue_normalized_coupling.v1` |
| response element | `scnsim.response_element.v1` |
| Direct operator | `scnsim.direct_operator.v1` |
| full HB response | `scnsim.hb_response.josephsoncircuits.v1` |
| Direct CMA-ES | `scnsim.direct_cmaes.cmaes_jl_0_2_6_state_replay.v2` |

The CMA request additionally fixes
`box_transform_id="cmaes-jl-0.2.6-linquad-unit-box.v1"`. Changed numerical or
replay semantics require a new ID. The outer CMA ID transitively binds the
exact CMAEvolutionStrategy.jl release and registry tree, Julia patch,
`minimize()` call and stop configuration, box transform, raw/transformed
population hash encoding, candidate compile/Direct/objective algorithm IDs,
continuation projection and boundaries, replay order, and winner/tie rule.
Changing any bound dependency requires a new outer ID even when the public
`CMAESSpec` fields do not change.

Source values and units from the executed attempt remain receipt evidence, but
only the coherent-SI bits, canonical SI unit, and dimensionality enter Plan or
request semantic identity. Thus `92 * u.fF` and `0.092 * u.pF` may reuse one
verified computation. Reuse does not append a second provenance event merely
to log the later caller's equivalent spelling.

## Give each file one job

| File | Required identity content | Mutability |
|---|---|---|
| `workspace.json` | one leaf binding, a replaceable root's active-leaf pointer, or a versioned Plan-to-iteration index, all with evidence-only instance IDs | mutable only at a root under the workspace lock; immutable in a leaf |
| `plan.json` | complete authored topology, recursive component snapshots, ordered identities, baselines, and catalog sources | immutable |
| `request.json` | Plan hash, operation, Ref lineage, Spec, ParameterSet, and semantic runtime | immutable |
| `attempt.json` | request hash, ordinal, allocation time, allocated/launched state, executable, resume-ledger, and state-appropriate machine evidence | finalized once after the launch bootstrap; immutable |
| `outcome.json` | Julia-staged request/attempt/runtime binding, terminal status, typed result/failure, and artifact inventory | immutable staging authority |
| `result.json` | typed Direct, quantity, optimization, or HB-batch result | immutable |
| `receipt.json` | request, attempt, Result/artifact hashes, source-unit/provenance evidence, and terminal outcome | written last; immutable |
| generation ledger | one complete CMA-ES generation, package-visible coordinates and hashes, candidate outcomes, continuation certificate, and previous-ledger hash | immutable artifact |
| artifact manifest | one Zarr artifact ID plus its complete ordered regular-file inventory | immutable artifact |
| bootstrap-ready record | request/ordinal binding plus actual Julia and BLAS evidence | exactly one transient stdout JSONL record before launch authorization |
| launch authorization | request hash plus finalized attempt hash | exactly one transient stdin JSONL record |
| progress record | non-authoritative completed-generation status bound to one request and attempt | transient JSONL only |

The bundle is the one closed full-V1 envelope set for every public component,
Plan, Ref/View lineage, Direct quantity, optimization, HB, Result, inventory,
attempt, artifact, and receipt surface described by the Contract. It is
deliberately broader than the first executable `dev3` slice: a later-slice
discriminator remains fail-fast until its runtime slice arrives, but reaching
`dev4` through `dev6` does not require inventing another schema version. The
`dev4` candidate now consumes the Composite realization, including its
declaration-ordered `public_parameters`; later-slice discriminators remain
fail-fast until their runtime slice arrives.
Unknown or post-V1 discriminators never fall through to a generic map.

JSON Schema enforces each envelope's shape. Cross-document semantic validation
then verifies the complete chain before reuse or `resolve()`:

- a replaceable root points to `leaves/<leaf-instance-id>` and repeats that
  leaf's instance ID and Plan hash;
- a leaf `workspace.json` names the SHA-256 of its exact `plan.json` bytes;
- every versioned index entry names a child directory whose leaf workspace and
  Plan hashes match that entry;
- `requests/<sha256>/` is named by its exact `request.json` hash, whose Plan hash
  matches the leaf Plan;
- a retained lineage names one exact Public node partition; when that terminal
  coordinate is not uniquely Port-bound, every wave-only retain
  `evidenceMatrix` is exactly `0 x 0` and hashes the closed
  `scnsim.lineage_matrix` v1 envelope with
  `applicability=not_port_realizable`, its label, empty shape, and empty
  row-major Float64 list; source-boundary and de-embedding hashes similarly
  cover closed v1 not-applicable envelopes with no fabricated matrix members;
- when the coordinate is uniquely Port-bound, those same digests instead bind
  the actual $A_k$, $B_k$, $R_k$, $D_k$, $Q_k$, original-Port projectors, and
  omitted matched-load matrix; `port_realizable` must agree with that Plan
  attachment in either case;
- a positive attempt ordinal uses `str(ordinal).zfill(6)`: both final
  `attempts/<ordinal-text>/` and staging
  `attempts/.staging-<ordinal-text>-<uuid>/` therefore have at least six
  decimal digits without truncating larger ordinals;
- the staging suffix is lowercase canonical UUIDv4 text matching
  `[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-4[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}`;
- `attempt.json.ordinal_text`, `directory`, and `staging_directory` reproduce
  the canonical names above, its numeric `ordinal` matches the final directory,
  and that attempt names the enclosing request hash;
- `receipt.json` names the exact request and attempt hashes, and a success names
  the exact `result.json` hash;
- a completed Julia success or Julia-produced typed failure has staged
  `outcome.json` naming that same request, attempt, and semantic runtime, and
  its status/result/failure/artifact inventory matches the sealed receipt;
- when a receipt carries `outcome_sha256`, the final attempt contains the exact
  valid `outcome.json` bytes with that hash; without that field, no authoritative
  `outcome.json` may exist under its final name;
- success and Julia-produced typed-failure receipts require that hash;
  `BackendProtocolError` from allocated process/bootstrap failure or from a
  missing/invalid envelope may omit it, and an interrupted attempt records it
  only when a valid envelope existed;
- the Result discriminator matches the request operation and Spec:
  `solve_direct` to `direct_response`, `solve_hb` to `hb_batch`,
  `optimize_direct` to `optimization`, and `evaluate_direct` to exactly one of
  `diagonal_root`, `hybridized_pole`, `transfer_zero`,
  `residue_normalized_coupling`, `response_element`, or `operator`;
- every successful HB case has an ordered `state_node_map` whose length equals
  the `states` artifact's second axis, whose `state_index` values equal their
  zero-based array positions, and whose `compiler_node_id` values reproduce the
  compiler node order and the state artifact's node-axis values;
- each `state_node_map.source` resolves against the sealed Plan hash: a
  `plan_node` names one Plan node with exact `public` or `port_promoted`
  visibility, a `component_private` names one frozen snapshot node by
  segment-array `component_path` plus `private_node_id`, and an
  `anonymous_internal` carries only the endpoint-derived full-digest
  `internal-<sha256>` audit ID;
- the receipt artifact list exactly matches the Result catalogs and manifest
  hashes before any artifact is opened.

Artifact IDs are unique within every inventory and bind one-to-one across
outcome, Result, and receipt. A request directory may contain at most one
verified success receipt; any competing success is corruption rather than a
winner selected by timestamp.

Every Zarr catalog entry names an artifact manifest with the same artifact ID;
the entry's SHA-256 is the hash of those exact canonical manifest bytes. The
manifest file is stored outside the Zarr directory, so it never inventories or
hashes itself.

Validation also enforces ordered/unique identities, matching retained/spec
coordinates, physical dimensionality, artifact IDs, and the versioned-index
invariants described by their owning contracts. Any mismatch is corrupt or
stale evidence, never a nearby Result or retry target.

Large arrays are not embedded in JSON. Each `array_catalog` entry requires a
relative Zarr path, SHA-256, media type, dtype, shape, axes, and unit;
`scalar_catalog` stores the exact fields required by its Result discriminator.
A regular-file artifact hashes its raw bytes. A directory-backed Zarr artifact
hashes a canonical JSON manifest of every contained regular file: NFC-normalized
POSIX-relative path, constant `regular` mode, byte length, and raw-byte SHA-256, sorted by
path. The directory's own name and empty directories are excluded; symlinks and
normalization collisions fail closed. Python and Julia therefore verify the
same metadata-and-chunk byte set rather than a filesystem-dependent directory
encoding.
A Direct response requires four fixed artifact groups:
`artifacts/frequencies.zarr`, `artifacts/s.zarr`, `artifacts/y.zarr`, and
`artifacts/z.zarr`, with correspondingly fixed artifact IDs and external
manifest names. Every group is Zarr V2 with little-endian Float64, C order,
`compressor=null`, `filters=null`, `fill_value=null`, and dot-separated chunk
keys. The frequency group contains the real dataset `values`; each matrix group
contains the paired datasets `real` and `imag`.

Julia is the sole writer of those Zarr trees. Each artifact root is a group
whose `.zgroup` bytes are exactly `{"zarr_format":2}` with no newline. A dataset
directory is an array, not another group, and its `.zarray` bytes are exactly
the lexicographically keyed, compact, no-newline form below after substituting
the declared positive decimal dimensions. For grid length $F$ and selected
coordinate count $N$, let $c=c(F)=\min(F,1024)$.

```text
{"chunks":[c],"compressor":null,"dimension_separator":".","dtype":"<f8","fill_value":null,"filters":null,"order":"C","shape":[F],"zarr_format":2}
```

```text
{"chunks":[c,N,N],"compressor":null,"dimension_separator":".","dtype":"<f8","fill_value":null,"filters":null,"order":"C","shape":[F,N,N],"zarr_format":2}
```

An HB selected matrix keeps coordinate-major/mode-minor order explicitly. With
output/input coordinate counts $N_o,N_i$ and output/input mode counts
$M_o,M_i$, its real and imaginary datasets flatten each channel to one ordered
`(coordinate, mode)` pair. Let $Q_o=N_oM_o$ and $Q_i=N_iM_i$; the datasets use:

```text
{"chunks":[c,Qo,Qi],"compressor":null,"dimension_separator":".","dtype":"<f8","fill_value":null,"filters":null,"order":"C","shape":[F,Qo,Qi],"zarr_format":2}
```

`frequencies.zarr` contains only root `.zgroup`, `values/.zarray`, and the
required `values/<chunk-index>` files. Each of `s.zarr`, `y.zarr`, and
`z.zarr` contains only root `.zgroup`, `real/.zarray`, `imag/.zarray`, and the
required dot-separated chunk files below those two datasets. Successful HB
case S/Y/Z and backend-native-S/Z artifacts use that same root-plus-real/imag
layout with their flattened three-dimensional shape. `.zattrs`,
`.zmetadata`, dataset `.zgroup` files, codecs, sidecars, extra files, and extra
directories are forbidden. Python validates the exact metadata bytes, complete
tree, chunk names and lengths, manifest, and hashes; it never opens the tree in
write mode or normalizes Julia's metadata.

An `OperatorResult` requires artifact ID `frequencies` at
`artifacts/frequencies.zarr` with manifest
`artifacts/frequencies.manifest.json`, plus artifact ID `operator` at
`artifacts/operator.zarr` with manifest
`artifacts/operator.manifest.json`. The latter uses the same complex `[F,N,N]`
metadata above, unit `siemens / second`, and chunk policy
`frequency_slab_full_matrix_v1`.

A successful HB case with minimum-six-digit ordinal text stores selected
`s`, `y`, `z`, `backend_native_s`, and `backend_native_z` groups beneath
`artifacts/cases/<case-ordinal-text>/`. Its `states` operating-point evidence is
`artifacts/cases/<case-ordinal-text>/states.zarr` with corresponding
`.manifest.json`, complex `weber` values, and chunk policy
`single_complete_array_v1`. Those values are SCNSim `exp(-i omega t)`
node-flux coefficients exposed through the case's `.states` property; the
complex artifact uses the same root-plus-real/imag layout at its declared state
shape. The adapter derives them from the fixed backend $x_{\mathrm{JC}}^+$ as
$\Phi^- = \varphi_0\operatorname{conj}(x_{\mathrm{JC}}^+)$ while
`returnnodeflux=false`; raw backend state and normalization remain
reconciliation evidence only, and no second node-flux array is requested or
published.

For $M_p$ ordered operating-point modes and $N_n$ compiled node coordinates,
both state datasets use axes `(pump_mode, node_coordinate)` and exact metadata:

```text
{"chunks":[Mp,Nn],"compressor":null,"dimension_separator":".","dtype":"<f8","fill_value":null,"filters":null,"order":"C","shape":[Mp,Nn],"zarr_format":2}
```

The successful `hbCaseOutcome` carries the required `state_node_map`; a failed
outcome carries neither it nor artifacts. The map is canonical Result JSON, not
a separate artifact or selector registry. Its bytes therefore enter the
`result.json` SHA-256 named by the success receipt, while the states manifest
and artifact hashes independently bind the array bytes. Cross-document
validation joins those chains by requiring the map, compiler basis, state node
axis, sealed Plan or Composite snapshot source, and array shape to agree.
Neither the axis kind nor a map entry creates a selectable state type:
`NetworkViewRef`, `retain()`, `transform_pair()`, and `CurrentDrive.at` keep
their existing closed selectors, and anonymous Internal nodes remain audit-only.

Frequency uses chunk shape
`[c(F)]`; matrix artifacts use `[c(F), N, N]`. Frequency has unit
`hertz`; S is `dimensionless`, Y is `siemens`, and Z is `ohm`. The manifest
still records ordered coordinate IDs, axis references, and probe-load state.
Alternative chunking is a schema/algorithm extension, not a writer-selected
option.

Direct response and Operator matrix axes reference artifact ID `frequencies`;
they do not repeat frequency values inline. HB case matrices and trace axes
instead reference the sealed request field `spec.frequencies`, because HB has
one request-global grid and no per-case frequency artifact. Coordinate, mode,
channel, and node axes carry their exact ordered labels inline. Semantic
validation requires every referenced axis length and ordering to match its
array shape.

An HB matrix analogously chunks the whole selected channel matrix per
frequency as `[c(F), N_o*M_o, N_i*M_i]`; it does not split one frequency's
channel matrix. Its axes are `(frequency, output_channel, input_channel)`.
Both channel-label arrays contain exact `(coordinate, mode)` pairs in
coordinate-major/mode-minor order. `MatrixView.matrix` exposes this stored
stack without an implicit reshape. The HB lattice stores one scalar
`signed_frequency` for each operating-point mode, but every input/output
response mode stores an ordered `signed_frequency_grid`. Semantic validation
requires that grid to equal
`spec.frequencies[k] + sum_j(mode[j] * pump_axes[j].frequency)` at every index,
to have the same length and order as `spec.frequencies` and the matrix leading
dimension, and to contain no zero response frequency. These values determine
the per-grid-point normalization, same-frequency permutation, and
reconciliation identity.

Semantic validation requires the four artifacts to share the same positive
$F$ and $N$, and each matrix's coordinate and probe-load lists to name exactly
the same ordered selected coordinates. It also checks the fixed artifact
ID/path against the matching manifest before receipt sealing and again on
`resolve()`.

A diagonal-root quantity requires root, frequency, linewidth, and slope
scalars; every other Direct quantity discriminator requires its own closed
scalar catalog. An optimization result
requires the successful baseline outcome, a winner, completed-generation count,
unused budget, and the complete hash-linked ledger inventory. Each successful
ledger objective component carries its evaluated Quantity, signed normalized
residual, and weighted cost so the request-owned target, resolved scale/source,
and weight reproduce the total. Semantic validation requires exactly one
component for every request objective, in request order, with matching unique
objective IDs. A success receipt requires the Result hash.
Failure receipts require a closed typed failure; interruption receipts require
explicit interruption evidence. Neither may advertise a Result.
Every failure evidence envelope also names the owning operation and carries its
stage-specific canonical context; category/kind/operation mismatches fail
semantic validation.

`ParameterRef` identity is always the ordered pair `(component_path,
parameter_id)`. A request carries the complete resolved binding for every Plan
parameter: explicit values override the sealed baseline, and omitted values are
expanded from that baseline before hashing. Bindings sort by this pair and must
be unique.

Each population candidate stores the callback-visible raw CMA sample as
`optimizer_latent_coordinates_f64` and its transformed unit-box sample as
`optimizer_coordinates_f64`. Physical values or transformed coordinates alone
cannot reconstruct the raw bits during retry because the package box transform
is many-to-one. Generation ledgers carry no serialized private Julia optimizer
object; deterministic replay is defined by the optimization implementation
contract.

Every optimization variable serializes immutable `model_default_bounds`, a
nullable `consumer_override_bounds`, and resolved `lower`/`upper` Quantities.
The resolved interval equals the override when present and otherwise the model
default. `optimizationSpec.allow_extrapolation` is sorted and unique by
`ParameterRef` identity and contains only active variables. Both bound roles,
resolved values, and the authorization list enter request identity. Candidate
and winner ParameterSets require empty `allow_extrapolation`; candidate
`extrapolation_evidence` uses only `none` or `optimization_spec`, while ordinary
receipt evidence uses only `parameter_set`. Cross-document validation checks
each evidence entry against the exact affine consumer, support interval,
resolved input value, side, nonnegative distance, and owning request.
It also requires exactly one entry for every out-of-support fan-out and no entry
for an in-support fan-out, including `none` evidence for a rejected candidate.
The entry's distance has the input/support dimensionality and equals
`support_lower - input_value` for `side=lower` or
`input_value - support_upper` for `side=upper` in coherent SI; it must be
strictly positive.

In population-column order, the canonical `[n, lambda]` raw matrix hashes to
`raw_optimizer_population_sha256`, and the matching transformed unit-box matrix
hashes to `transformed_optimizer_population_sha256`. The hashes cover the
canonical Float64-bit matrix encoding, including declared shape and order, and
must reproduce the candidate arrays in that ledger. They bind what the package
callback exposed (`y`) separately from what physical evaluation consumed (`z`);
neither hash may be reconstructed from physical parameter values.

Every generation ledger also binds a closed continuation certificate. Its
`completed_generation` must equal the ledger generation; nonfinal generations
use `post_update_post_next_sample_pre_next_update` and require
`next_raw_optimizer_population_sha256` plus
`next_transformed_optimizer_population_sha256` for the next sampled matrices.
The request's last generation uses `terminal_post_update` and forbids both next
hashes. Cross-file semantic validation rejects another boundary, missing or
unexpected next hashes, or a certificate projection ID that differs from the
one transitively bound by the request algorithm identity.

For a Direct grid of length $F$ and selected coordinate count $N$, frequency
has shape `[F]`; S, Y, and Z each have shape `[F, N, N]` with axes ordered as
frequency, output coordinate, input coordinate. All three matrix artifacts use
the same ordered coordinate IDs and load-state mapping. Cross-document
validation checks those lengths, axis references, and the dimensionless/siemens/ohm
units before constructing a Result.

## Keep evidence out of semantic identity

Request identity excludes workspace location, source-unit spelling,
presentation theme, schematic ground grouping, progress display, attempt
ordinal, host, executable path, CPU, and thread counts. Those facts remain
auditable in the workspace and attempt evidence.

Each replaceable root, concrete leaf, and versioned parent receives a lowercase
canonical UUIDv4 `workspace_instance_id` using the same text form required for
the staging nonce. A Run binds the leaf ID as well as its Plan hash. A
replacement creates a new leaf ID, so an old Run remains stale even if later
iterations produce the same Plan hash again; the UUID is evidence only and
never enters Plan or request identity.

The workspace is an evidence location, not a request namespace. Relocating an
intact workspace does not rename its requests. Conversely, copying one
`request.json` without its verified receipt and artifacts cannot materialize a
Result.

This hash chain detects stale, partial, mismatched, and accidentally corrupted
evidence under the ordinary local-workspace trust model. It is not a signature
scheme and does not claim resistance to an adversary able to rewrite every file
and recompute every hash. V1 adds no signing or external attestation service.
